title: DCR - Want to change typeahead strategy for read-only combo boxes
description: in our application ; selecting a choice in a combo box causes some back-end processing.  So we want to be careful on the selections within a combo box.  In a combo box that has many choices the user would like to type the first few chars of an item.  The read-only selects based only on the first letter that was typed.  This forces an implementation of a typeahead solution based on key listeners.  None of this works with key listeners of course because the combo is always selecting the first letter.  So if you type ahead 2 chars ; if will actually fire a selection event 3 times; before arriving at the correct choice.  And as you can imagine selecting three times ; slows down the combo box due to the backend processing.

title: [Import/Export] On MacOS X SWT Buttons easily get wrong height
description: I20030605; MacOS 10.2.6; ; The Aqua (look&feel of MacOS X) UI guidelines clearly define the height of (standard) ; oval shaped buttons.; However; in Eclipse there are lots of places where these buttons have a non-standard ; height and look ugly (because the left and right sides are no longer semi-circular but look ; more like round-cornered rectangles). See attached screenshots.; ; I think there should be some mechanism (or just a constant) in Platform UI that help Non-; Mac developers to get the height right.

title: [GlobalActions] GlobalUndoAction / GlobalRedoAction causes NPE by unsafely disposing old delegate
description: Build ID: I20080523-0100; ; Steps To Reproduce:; My GMF (1.0.3 ) based diagram editor shows program call graph. Node represents a procedure in a source code; line represents a call relationship. User can double click a node to open the source code in a LPEX text editor.  A NPE occurs if user does some tasks involving opening source in text editor; closing it;  switching back and forth between text editor and diagram editor. It happens randomly but can frequently reproduced with the interaction which intertwines PartServices firePartActivated; firePartClosed events. For example:; ; 1. launch the diagram; 2. double click on a node representing a procedure from source file A to automatically open source A in a text editor; 3. close the text editor and switch back to the diagram; 4. double click on another node representing a procedure from A to open the editor for A.; 5. switch back to diagram editor; 6. double click on a node from source file B to open source file B; 7. close text editor for source B and switch back to diagram ; 8. double click on another node representing a procedure form source file B to open source file B; ; A NPE is thrown because OperationHistoryActionHandler$PartListener has a null site when calling partClosed(). ; title: Preventing second session on same workspace does not work on Linux
description: For preventing workspace corruption; a .lock file is written in the .metadata ; directory of the workspace.; ; The code for preventing a second session of Eclipse in Main.java of startup ; code and org.eclipse.core.internal.runtime.InternalPlatform#createLockFile() is ; such that ; ; 1) you delete the .lock file ; 2) if the deletion fails; then another session is running on the same workspace; 3) if the deletion succeeds; then no other session is using the workspace; ; ; This is done by using File.delete(). On Windows; this delete fails and thus a ; second session is prevented from running.; ; But on Linux; File.delete() succeeds irrespective of a file handle being open ; on the file. I have tested this with JDK1.4.2. ; ; For this to work; the check should be done only on the existence of the file ; and not deleting it. ; ; To ensure that .lock file is deleted even when JVM is abnormally terminated ; (like CTRL+C being pressed); a shutdown hook can be registered and the deletion ; of the .lock file can be done in the shutdown hook.

title: [context launching] Eclipse platform not able to pass all input file selections to the debug launch shortcut
description: Build ID: 3.3 GA; ; Steps To Reproduce:; Scenario: Our launch configuration requires multiple files as input. When multiple files are selected and the bug button (icon) is pressed; the platform is only able to pass the first file to the launch shortcut. So the user will be asked again for the path(s) of the other file(s) when invoking our launch shortcut. ; ; The code that might be responsible for this behavior is in the protected IResource getSelectedResource0() method in SelectedResourceManager.java in the org.eclipse.debug.internal.ui.stringsubstitution package. In this method; the selection (which contains multiple files at this point) is casted into an instance of type IStructuredSelection named ss. Only the first element in ss will be initiated into an Object o; and this object named o then gets casted into an instance of type IResource called resource. And resource will be returned to the calling method and eventually be used to extract the file paths. As only the first element actually gets returned; so the other file paths will be lost before they are passed to the launch shortbut. As a result; our launch shortbut is not able to create a launch configuration properly and is forced to ask the user for input again.; ; Expected behavior: all of the selections should be properly stored and passed on to the next function. The user should not be asked for input files again if he/she already selected them; and a debug session should start given the inputs.; ; ; ; More information:

title: setEnabled for Composite or Group

I think this method should be reimplemented in composite to deal with children controls.; ; Another problem is that some child controls from group are not disabled visualy even when setEnabled(false) is called for them.

title: Search ignores .cvsignore
description: I did a search for a string in my plugin development workspace (Search > Search > File Search); and got a huge error list of files that were supposedly out of sync with the repository.  The files on the list seemed to be files that I had excluded using .cvsignore.; ; It seems only logical to me that if Eclipse is going to complain about a file being out of synch; it should make sure that file isnt excluded via .cvsignore first.; ; This is obviously not a work stopping problem; just an inconvenience that might be confusing to some.; ; Thanks!

title: [content assist] auto-activated and manual assist collide when assist cycling is enabled
description: N20060418; ; - see also bug 109594; - type a field name and a dot; triggering auto-activated content assist; and press Ctrl+Space; ; > sometimes; if the keyboard shortcut comes in after the autoactivation; the completion popup continues to the second page when multiple categories are enabled. This is misleading.; ; A good way to illustrate the problem is after starting up eclipse. Typing the dot will start auto-activated assist; but computing the proposals after start up will take a while; with the manual invocation waiting in the message pump. When the proposals are finally displayed; the popup switches to the second page immediately.; ; The solution does not count manual content assist invocation that occur within a grace period after the last auto-activated invocation.; ; The length of the grace period is the auto-activation delay; but never less than 200ms.

At this point the refresh is partially complete;; but the navigator has not yet received a delta for it. When the content provider; asks for the children of the project; it gets a list of the folders that have; already been discovered. Say the project P contains single folder f at this; point. The folder f is shown in the navigator.  At this point the children of; f have not yet been discovered; so no plus box is added for the f tree; item. (hasChildren returns false at this point).; 4) The refresh completes; and WorkbenchContentProvider receives a delta for all; of the refresh resources. title: Default external web browser not found when running 32-bit Eclipse on 64-bit Ubuntu 9.04
description: CQ:WIND00185536; ; BuildId: Eclipse-3.5.1-GTK 32-bit; Host: Ubuntu Desktop Edition 9.04; 64-bit with Sun 1.5.0_11 32-bit VM; ; The default external web browser (Firefox) is not found when running 32-bit Eclipse on 64-bit Ubuntu. This is a problem for our product; because as a result the Help system is not working; and also the internal browser is not working.; ; Workaround: ; Edit Window > Preferences > General > Web Browser to register a proper external web browser. The problem with this is; that due to bug 293159; finding the proper external web browser is nontrivial.; ; Engineering Details:; This behavior seems to be caused by missing 32Bit gnome libraries on the 64Bit Ubuntu Host:; libgnomevfs-2.so.0 => not found; libgnome-2.so.0 => not found; libgnomeui-2.so.0 => not found; It seems that there are no 32Bit compatibility libraries available for this (at least I could not find any so far). As a result; the GTK default browser detection code fails.; ; Proposed Solution:; When detection of the System Browser via GTK libraries fails; Eclipse should check whether any of firefox; mozilla; netscape are found in the System PATH. Launching the external browser does not require the GTK integration; if a browser is found in the system PATH.; ; Severity:; Not having a default external browser presents a severe limitation of initial out-of-the-box user experience. While the workaround is relatively easy from a technical point of view; that workaround does present a problem to end users. Therefore; if there is an acceptable technical solution for this (e.g. as proposed); it should be fixed. See also bug 288140; bug 286314; bug 291885; and bug 293159 for related issues.

title: Preference performance regression
description: Build: I20050413; ; This build introduced a significant regression in the performance of retreiving; preferences from a large preference node.  This is due to a switch from; java.util.Properties to our internal ObjectMap class.  ObjectMap uses linear; lookup rather than hashing; and so degrades linearly as the size of the table; grows.  This results in lookups that are an order of magnitude slower when; reading; for example; JDT core preferences; which have several hundred; preferences per preference node.

title: Ability to Build and Run in one click
description: A simple button on the toolbar that allows the user to both Build the current project and Run the compiled executables at once would be greatly appreciated. As trivial as it may sound; constant recompiling and rerunning of large projects would be greatly sped up if the executable would be run immediately after the compiling had completed; because the user could then press the one button then move onto other things whilst waiting for it to compile all the while knowing that the project will boot up for them once it s finished.

title: [Themes] [JFace] FontRegistry doc needs more detail on font dispose handling by clients
description: Ive noticed that the FontRegistry can dispose of fonts; but it does not ; explain in its documentation when this can happen and what steps a client ; should take to handle these situations.; ; For example; the put method on FontRegistry will dispose the old font if one ; had been recreated. Before the font is disposed; all listeners are notified of ; the pending font change. We should warn clients of this. It would seem to mean ; that clients that get any fonts from the FontRegistry must add themselves as ; listeners and when a font change is sent to them; get the new font. Or maybe we ; just never dispose of the fonts except when the Display is about to be disposed?; ; Whatever way we decide to take; we need to document this so the client is not ; left holding onto a disposed font.

title: [Net] ui.net can cause the instance location to be set to default too early
description: See bug306816 comment 24; ; The bundle org.eclipse.ui.net uses an activator that extends AbstractUIPlugin.  The issue here is that the AbstractUIPlugin is using legacy preferences in the stop(BundleContext context) method to save the preference store.  ; ; First of all; I dont believe ui.net stores anything in the instance preference store so saving the preference store should not be necessary.  This ends up loading the legacy preferences to get loaded and the instance area to be set to the default location if it was not already set.  To solve this immediate issue could we consider overriding AbstractUIPlugin.savePreferenceStore() to do nothing?; ; I admit that will only solve this one usage of AbstractUIPlugin and the usage of legacy preferences.  ; ; DJ; I think we have another preference bug(s) that complain about preferences causing the setting of the instance area too soon.  Perhaps this is a dup of that bug if it exists?

title: [Bidi] Need to extend BidiSegmentListener
description: Currently; BidiSegmentListener provides means of Bidi segmentation aimed at preserving the relative order of text runs.; ; Thats a highly valuable function; broadly consumed in Bidi-enabled SW products.; ; However; preserving order of segments is just one kind of Bidi overrides.; ; I think that with a very small effort we could make Bidi segments support more comprehensive and flexible.; (The expected changes may be considered API related though.); ; At present; we allow clients to communicate to the layout engine segment offsets; whereas characters applied at these offsets are fixed (well; fixed per paragraph direction) and hardcoded in TextLayout.; ; In order to accomplish any variation to the Bidi algorithm; we just need to let clients also choose code points to be inserted at those offsets.; ; A sound use case in this context is visually stored data (practiced e.g. on mainframe systems); which requires nonstandard reordering action.; The desired appearance of such data in system environments lacking out of box support for treating data as visual (e.g. MS Windows) can be achieved by use of control characters LRO/RLO (U+202C/U+202D).; ___________; ; More information:; ; If BidiSegmentListener enhancements sound acceptable in principle; I can post a detailed proposal of the expected code/API changes.

title: Eclipse should support alpha/beta/milestone releases
description: Another way to put this is; update should work for milestone releases.; ; Currently; a plugin/feature version number must be an integer three-tuple (major; version; minor version; incremental version). This is inadequate for real; software projects; as evidenced by the fact that when Eclipse itself goes into; its milestone cycles; it stops using version number for anything but the target; release and instead identifies versions by build numbers. This is the reason; that update doesnt work for milestones (which is something of a FAQ).; ; The current hierarchical scheme needs only a slight modification to handle; beta/milestone releases. For example; suppose you added an optional fourth; integer to the series; indicating a beta version. Then:; ; 3.1.0.10 > 3.1.0.9; ; But:; ; 3.1.0 > 3.1.0.10; ; This is not rocket science and would add a very useful capability to Eclipse;; one that better models what actually happens in the real world.

title: Enhance PluginConverter API
description: In order to take some of the load off the runtime and the too-strong -clean ; when self-hosting; PDE needs to generate manifest.mf for workspace plugins ; that undergo changes undetected by the runtime (e.g. addition of new packages) ; from one launch to the next. (bug 75213); ; The current API is not sufficient:; PluginConverter.convertManifest(File; boolean; String; boolean) is not ; sufficient for this scenario.  This is because the last arg (ie. analyzeJars) ; only works on JARs. ; ; We need to be able to make a call on the plugin converter that will behave as ; it would when the runtime starts up in dev mode.  That is; we need the plugin ; converter to also look at all output folders; not just JARs.

title: Support for core variables
description: Currently; all variable support exists in Debug UI and the support; is tied to the UI.; ; From the Debug mailing list (author DarinW):; One of our intentions is to add support for launch variables to the ; debug platform. This allows for various launch configurations to reuse the ; variable implemetation and share variables across different types of ; launch configurations. For example; a common use of variables is to define ; user-specific paths; such as ${CATALINA_HOME}. The variable is shared on ; the launch config; and each user can define their workstation specific ; value.; ; The notion of variables will be defined in the debug platform. There will ; be two types of variables:; (1) Simple variables. A simple variable has an identifier and a value that ; does not change (or at least does not change often). Such a variable could ; be defined by a user in a preference page; or could be contributed by an ; extension (i.e. plug-ins can contribute variables). A variable contributed ; by an extension may define either a default value for the variable; or ; provide an initializer. An initializer is a delegate class that will be ; instantiated by the debug plug-in; when required; to obtain the ; initial/default value of the variable.; (2) Context sensitive variables. A context sensitive variable has an ; identifier and has a dynamic value. A context sensitive variable will be ; contributed via an extension; and provide a resolver that can bind a ; value to the variable; given a launch context (i.e. a launch ; configuration). A context sensitive variable may have arguments. It is up ; to the resolver to interpret the arguments in a launch context. A resolver ; may require a UI; or may not - it is up to the contributor.; ; The debug platform will provide utilities for resolving variable values; ; identifing arguments; etc.; ; The debug UI will provide facilities for the presentation/editing of ; variables:; (1) A preference page will be provided to create user-defined (simple) ; variables; and assign values to (simple) variables.; (2) A dialog will be provided for selecting one or more variables from a ; list. This will be useful for launch configuration tabs that allow the use ; of variables. The dialog will allow variables to contribute a UI component ; where applicable. For example; a variable that binds to a specific ; resource may provide a UI component to select a resource.; ; Launch delegates will be responsible for resolving variable values at ; launch time (using APIs provided by the debug platform). Since the places ; that variables may be specified in a launch configuration are ; launch/application specific; it will be up to launch configuration ; delegates to use the debug platform APIs to resolve variable values. If we ; can find ways to make this simpler (for example; pre-processing a launch ; config to bind values to variables); we will do so.

title: Ctrl+Tab cannot be entered on KeysPreferencePage
description: Ctrl+Tab can not be set as a key binding for any command/action using the new; incarnation of the KeysPreferencePage.  This is partly by design of the page;; and partly due to the nature of SWT.  This happens because the text widget; allows all tab traversal; and SWT treats Ctrl+Tab as a traversal operation in a; text widget.  This could be fixed either by SWT; or by the KeysPreferencePage; itself.

title: [Intro] Shared style design is too aggressive
description: Intro framework allows for specifying a shared style that will be injected in ; all Intro pages. This shared style is specified in the implementation element ; of the config.; We inject this shared style into all intro pages. However; this is too ; aggressive. There are usecases where the shared style can actually complicate ; the ease of the contribution. ; Usecase: contribute a page into a config; where the page has a style too ; similar to the original config. The framework injects the shared style at the ; topic of the style list of the page; but it is too hard to override that shared ; style if too many CSS attributes are similar with the shared. ; ; ; suggested solution: add an attribute to a page definition that allows for ; disabling of the the shared style. ; eg:; <page style=pageStyle include-shared-style=false .... /> ; ; the flag indicates whether or not we need to inject the shared style; as ; opposed to the current behavior where we inject in each page by default.

title: [Table] TableColumn#pack() no longer respects TableItems Font
description: The following snippet puts an ... next to the TableItems content. It uses bold Font which requires a bit more space than normal Font; but a pack on the TableColumn does not respect that. The snippet works with M4 and before:; ; public class Main {;   public static void main(String[] args) {;     Display display = new Display();;     Shell shell = new Shell(display);;     shell.setLayout(new FillLayout());; ;     FontData def[] = display.getSystemFont().getFontData();; ;     Table t = new Table(shell; SWT.NONE);;     t.setHeaderVisible(true);; ;     TableColumn col = new TableColumn(t; SWT.NONE);;     col.setText(Hello);; ;     TableItem item = new TableItem(t; SWT.NONE);;     item.setText(Hello World);;     item.setFont(new Font(display; def[0].getName(); def[0].getHeight(); SWT.BOLD));; ;     col.pack();; ;     shell.open();;     while (!shell.isDisposed()) {;       if (!display.readAndDispatch()) {;         display.sleep();;       };     };   }; }; ; This currently blocks my next release unfortunately. I hoped being able to run with M5. A workaround is to set the bold Font on the entire Table. However; that would show any TableColumn in Bold as well.; ; Ben

title: random crashing; occurs in 3.2 and 3.1
description: I installed eclipse 3.1 in february; worked fine for several months; then suddenly started crashing randomly with increasing frequency until it became unusable.  Tried to reinstall 3.1; was able to run for a few days before it began crashing again with the same pattern.  Also tried different java versions; taking pains to be sure no other java version was use; and removed the only extra plugin we were using (Checkclipse).  I also know that my PC was configured for automatic updates.; ; I decided to try 3.2; so I installed it; it ran ok for about four days; then started to crash randomly as 3.1 had done; with the same increasing frequency.  Now it is crashing anywhere from 0 to 5 times an hour; and it often takes 2 or 3 restarts before I can begin work again.; ; When I say random crashing I mean that it crashes when rebuilding the workspace; when editing; and when manipulating the menus.  Sometimes it crashes just after the splash screen appears; and I have to kill the process.  It is also crashing when I am working in another application; and eclipse is seemingly idle.  Several times I have left the computer; come back; and found that Eclipse has crashed.  Many times the computer panics and shuts down.; ; I am surrounded by coworkers with the same machine and similar environment who have no trouble running their Eclipse of various versions; can find nothing out of place with my eclipse installation or project setup; I am using the same command line arguments they were.  I tried altering a number of options (-clean vs no -clean; memory; jvm; etc) with no observable change in behaviour (still crashes).; ; I thought that there may have been a problem with 3.1.0 and a windows update; but at least one of my coworkers runs 3.1.0 with her automatic windows updates enabled.; ; I dont have any chronic PC problems with other applications.  I am currently running 3.2 and Java 1.5.0.7; and haved tried 3.2 with 1.5.0.6; 1.4.2.12; 1.4.2.5.  I have also tried 3.1 with 1.5.0.6 and 1.4.2.5.  No combination seems to cause a working behaviour.; ; A quick browse through my growing collection of hs_err_pidXXXX.log files shows seemingly random problems on a variety of threads.; ; Please let me know what I can do further to assist you.  I like Eclipse very much and am anxious to use it soon without wondering when it will crash next.; ; Please let me know if there is a solution to this.

title: [Commands] ActionContributionItem isvisible should issue warning when action is not visible
description: 3.0; Ive spent a couple hours trying to figure out why a newly created action wasnt; showing up in the UI. There was nothing in the log and no error reported. The; problem can be reproduced as follows:; 1. create an retargetable action with a id; and an actionDefinitionId.; 2. add the action to a menu contribution manager; in my example it was added via; a workbench advisor to the main menu.; 3. when the menu manager fills the menu it checks if the action is visible;; because the action has an actionDefinitionId the visibility check verifies if; its associated command exists and is enabled; but the action doesnt have a; command so the action is not visible. ; ; At the minimum there should be a warning to the log that an action with a; definition id doesnt have an associated command. In addition; Im not sure that; actions in this state should be not be visible anyway. Just log the warning and; ignore the action definition id.

title: [CommonNavigator] Project Explorer and Link with editor causes continuous re-selecting of method name when changing signature
description: Setup:; ; - started Eclipse 3.3.2 with completely fresh workspace; - created new java project; - created a new class in any package; - using project explorer and enabling link with editor; - expanding the classs members in the project explorer; - opened the .java file for the new class in standard java editor in eclipse; - creating a new method; i.e. typing in public void test; ; --> beginning from here; eclipse will ALWAYS mark the method name of the new method whenever i do anything that would result in a change of the methods signature. It is irrelevant wether or not i pause shortly while typing or not.; ; The problem with this is that because of eclipse doing this WHILE i am trying to modify the method; the marking of the method while im typing will result in me deleting the method name with anything i was just typing in. The reason seems to be that the project explorer updates the tree view with the methods new siganture and then selects the (modified) method in the tree view. When this happens; the methods name is marked in the java editor; thus causing the problem.; ; This behaviour is specific to the project explorer (package explorer will update and select the method in the tree view; but will NOT mark the method name in the java editor); which i need to use because i need to be able to open and edit uml2 models in eclipse. So anytime i forget switching back to the package explorer; this problem can hit me.; ; It took me several weeks just to identify the problem being caused by the project explorer with enabled link to editor and expanded class members; until then it nearly drove me crazy (again and again deleting method names while just wanting to change their siganture; AND not knowing why it happens ;-) ). I also cannot see how the described behaviour could in any way be a desired one - this just seems like a bug to me; thats why im reporting it here.; ; I hope my descriptions were sufficient;; ; thx Thomas

title: [Browser] Download same file fails after cancel twice
description: [env]; * RedHat EL4 WS Update 4; * Eclipse 3.3 M4 build. ; * Firefox 1.5.0.8; [Steps to reproduce]; 0. Open Internet Web Browser view.; 1. Open a download link to download the file; the file save dialog will show and [Cancel] the dialog;; 2. Open the URL like www.googel.com then search a word like Eclipse; open a link in the search result web page; then popup a new WebBrowser in the new Shell;; 3. Do not close the new WebBrowser Shell window; select Internet Web Browser; press Back in the first WebBrowser to the first download link used in the Step one.; 4. Clink on the same download link used in Step one; then the file save dialog will show and [Cancel] the dialog the second time;; 5.  Clink on the same download link used in Step one; then the file save dialog will not show and can not do download this file anymore.; ; [Expected:]; It should show the File save dialog.; ; [More]; 1. Step2 is in order to show a second browser instance. We found after Step2; it can easily reproduce the problem.; 2. Some found:;   * Type about:config to show the Mozilla config;   * Search cache in the Filter input.;   * Find browser.cache.memory.enable config item; change value to False. ;  After it changes to False; it always can pop up the download dialog. ; 3. It doesnt affect other download links; only that link cannot work.

title: [Import/Export] Suggestions for the export wizard
description: File -> export...; ; This dialog shows a lot of options; and its hard to determine what to pick.; This is difficult because some of the options identify file formats; some of the; options identify what will be stored in those files. ; ; For example; if the user wants to export an Eclipse plugin to work on it in; another workspace; they may want to export a Deployable plug-in and fragment; in a Jar File which is known to be an Archive File stored on the File; System... so its not obvious which option to select. (I know what these; options mean now; but I didnt when I first encountered the wizard years ago).; ; I would suggest the following:; ; ; SPLITTING THE WIZARD INTO 3 PARTS:; ; 1. An Export... wizard that strictly copies the raw contents of the workspace; to a different location. This would include the current Archive file and File; System options and should probably also include the team Share Project and; Commit options. (optional) These wizards could potentially be accessed using; an Export action on the IResource context menu.; ; 2. A Build... wizard that strictly builds new things from the contents of the; workspace. This would include the Deployable Features; Deployable plug-ins; and fragments; Ant Buildfiles; Javadoc; etc. It should probably also; include the CVS create patch option.; ; 3. Options that export application settings. This currently only applies to; Preferences; but could potentially include options to export a perspective;; workbench layout; etc. These would export settings that control how Eclipse (or; the RCP app) behaves; but not the users work. These should be accessed from the; whatever bit of UI the user normally goes to when they change these settings; (such as the preferences dialog; the customize perspective dialog; etc.); ; ; REORGANIZING THE EXPORT WIZARD:; ; All the wizards that export the raw workspace (the wizard thats still called; Export...; above) should be rearranged. First the user should be asked What; do you want to export and then they should be asked What format do you want to; export it in?. ; ; The What do you want to export page should be generic and pluggable. Its; output would be a set of IResources that then get passed to the What format; wizard that is separately pluggable. This means that no matter what format you; want to export in; the UI for selecting the bits of the workspace should remain; the same. ; ; The SDK should ship with (at least) 2 options in the What to export page.; ; 1. Files and projects from the workspace (contributed by o.e.ui.ide); ; This would contain a file selector similar to what currently shows up under; Archive file; etc.; ; 2. All files shared in CVS (contributed by the team UI); ; This would export everything that isnt listed in .cvsignore. (Thus allowing; people to export everything that would normally be synchronized with CVS in; whatever format they wish).

title: SearchForBuildFilesDialog.searchForBuildFiles optimization
description: From Eclipse-dev:; ; In todays integration build (20030114); there is new API in the ; org.eclipse.core.resources plugin for performing optimized traversals of ; resource trees.  The optimization works by avoiding the creation of transient ; Path and IResource handles during the traversal of tree elements that you are ; not interested in visiting.  Instead; the visitor is given a resource proxy; ; from which various information can be obtained without any garbage being ; created.  The new API entry point is: ; ; IResource.accept(IResourceProxyVisitor; int). ; ; If you currently use IResourceVisitor; you should switch to the new API if any ; of the following is true: ; ;  - your visitor is not interested in every resource in the subtree being ; visited (for example; you only care about folders; files ending in .xml; ; derived resources; etc.). ; ; - your visitor only needs the simple resource name; or other simple information ; that is available from the resource proxy. ; ; - your visitor is interested in the full resource path; but doesnt need access ; to the resource handle ; ; If you dont already use IResourceVisitor; but you currently traverse ; significant subtrees using IContainer.members(); you may also benefit from ; switching to this new API.  One great example is code that traverses a subtree ; to count the number of resources in order to initialize a progress monitor (for ; example the method #countChildrenOf in most ExportOperation classes). description: I did a performance test on both Solaris 9 and Win2000 platform using the 3.0.2 ; build (M20041215). The procedure was as follows:; - Using the Plugin Development perspective. title: [Help] Allow help author to specify search description text in an html <meta/> tag
description: Currently; the help system scrapes the first 170 or so characters from an html page (starting after the first heading/line break or something like that apparently) to populate the description text in the search results. Often that works fine; but sometimes the author might want to supply his own text. For example; DITA supports a <shortdesc> element that allows the topic writer to write a short summary of the topic contents. This would probably be more accurate than the first 170 characters of the topic. Also; some pages may have javascript or header content before the real content. ; ; Theres a standard html meta tag for describing a pages content:; ; <meta name=description content=Describes how to sharpen and polish widgets./>; ; The help system should use the content of the content attribute from this meta tag if it exists and if not; fallback to the current method.

title: Double-click behavior should select on double-down; not double-up
description: Double-clicking selects a word in the eclipse text editor; but it is not following the ; Windows (or MacOS) rules for how that should work.; ; A double click consists of four steps:; 1.  Mouse Down (Ill call it single-down); 2.  Mouse Up  (Ill call it single-up); 3.  Mouse Down (Ill call it double-down); 4.  Mouse Up (Ill call it double-up); ; Eclipse currently selects the word that the single-down (or single-up?) was in on the ; double-up event.  It should do it on the double-down event; and allow the selection to be ; expanded by dragging between the double-down and double-up.; ; When step 3.5 Drag to select words is inserted in the above list; the selection should ; expand by whole words only; not by characters within words.

title: standaloneUpdate fails with Feature cannot be updated when no updates available
description: Version:  found with 3.1.2; verified in 3.2 GA; ; Details:; If you run the update manager from the UI and there are no updates available; you get a message that says No updates for the currently installed feature(s) found; try again later.:; ; If you run the update manager from the command line using standaloneUpdate; the command fails with an error and the log contains a message that says Feature {whatever} cannot be updated.; ; This makes it seem as if there is a fatal problem with either your command or your configuration; as opposed to there simply not being anything available yet.; ; To reproduce:; 1) Install eclipse 3.2 GA; 2) Start eclipse 3.2 IDE; select Help>Software Updates>Find and Install;Search for updates for currently installed features; take defaults; receive No updates available dialog; 3) Run standaloneUpdate from the eclipse folder;     $ java -cp startup.jar org.eclipse.core.launcher.Main -application org.eclipse.update.core.standaloneUpdate -command update -featureId org.eclipse.platform; 4) Receive the error; Command failed. Please check log file C:\Documents and Settings\hvanstee\workspace\.metadata\.log for details.; 5) Check the log; !ENTRY org.eclipse.update.core 4 0 2006-07-21 14:34:52.289; !MESSAGE Feature org.eclipse.platform cannot be updated.; ; Expected behavior:; - The message should say something to the effect of; !MESSAGE Feature org.eclipse.platform has no updates currently available; - The command should not indicate failure on return since this a normal condition until the first update is released.

title: Packaging for multiple platform support causes common code to be included multiple times.
description: This is a packaging request.  We have just gone through and packaged our ; product.  We include our feature with Eclipse and provide 7 installers; one for ; each supported platform.  This takes a great deal of disk space and is hard to ; manage.  Since most of the constituents are common - jar files; etc.; then I am ; wondering if it is possible to package the product as a super product.  This ; super product would have all the platform specific code kept separately for ; each platform and the common code only packaged once.  After installation; the ; user would invoke Eclipse by entering eclipse_win32; eclipse_solaris; or ; whatever.; ; It seems to me that this would reduce the size of Eclipse based products that ; support multiple platforms - although it would be larger than the installation ; for any single existing platform.

title: [Viewers] JFace StructuredViewer.preservingSelection ends up using Object.equals instead of comparer for comparing elements
description: StructuredViewer has a method setComparer(IElementComparer) to provide an; alternate means of comparing elements.  In my case; equals is a very deep (slow); comparison; so I use this feature to make my lists faster.  In particular; I am; using TableViewer.; ; However; when doing a StructuredViewer.refresh; when there is a selection in the; table; the function preservingSelection does:; ; if (!newSelection.equals(oldSelection)); ; And if you look at StructuredSelection.equals; it in turn compares the elements; using Object.equals.; ; I think it would be nice if this comparison could be done using the; IElementComparer of the StructuredViewer.  I have subclassed TableViewer to kind; of hack this in; but it would be nice if this functionality were already there.

title: [StyledText] StyledText Supplementary/Surrogate character navigation
description: Eclipse 3.0RC1; Sun JVM 1.4.2_03; ; Within a StyledText box paste in a Unicode supplementary character; for example; MATHEMATICAL_BOLD_CAPITAL_A with hexadecimal code point 1D400h:; <http://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U1D400.pdf>; You have to construct the character. I just used CLISP from the GNOME Terminal: ; (princ #\mathematical_bold_capital_a); ; I selected the character and pasted it into a StyledText box. In GTK without the; gylph being available this will appropriately display as a character with the; hexadecimal value in a rectangle:; [01D]; [400]; ; Now push the left arrow to attempt to move the caret before the character. Type; a character and the text disappears and nothing more typed is visible. This is; probably because the valid UTF-16 character composed of high and low 16 bit; surrogates has been split; creating an illegal UTF-16 sequence.; ; Inserting text is also affected after a supplementary character. Paste a; supplementary character then type abc. Press the left arrow and type some; additional letters. The caret doesnt move to before c even though letters are; inserted before c.; ; D800h to DFFFh are reserved for UTF-16 surrogate pairs and no code points are; assigned to them. This means each surrogate is individually distinguishable and; cannot be mistake for a single 16 bit code point.; ; Supplementary Characters in the Java Platform; <http://java.sun.com/developer/technicalArticles/Intl/Supplementary/>; ; Character navigation of supplementary Unicode characters within a StyledText box; should be feasible even without Java 1.5. It is going to be just as awkward to; implement in Java 1.5 because the char type is not being upgraded to a size that; will fit all Unicode code points. The number of code points in a Java string or; array of char can only be determined by parsing the entire string or array.; UTF-16 is a variable width encoding without the space advantage of UTF-8 nor the; fixed width advantage of UTF-32.; ; Regards;; Adam Warner

title: Support discovery of AWT Frames by walking the Widget hierarchy
description: There is no way to get a reference to an embedded AWT frame by walking the; SWT hierarchy. ; ( well there is some reference to the created frame that is kept internally; implicitely in the Listeners created internally by SWT_AWT; but that is the only; place.); ; This makes automating GUI tests impossible with tests frameworks when AWT is; embedded in SWT; since you cannot discover fully what your UI is made of.; Getting a reference to the embedded AWT object when walking the SWT hierarchy; would help quite a bit.; ; Mixed applications (a frequent use case for folks migrating from Swing to RCP); are not testable for now.; ; I dont know what could be the right solution that could be both portable and; clean; but here are some ideas:; Conceptually the AWT frame is a child of the composite is has been embedded in.; Potentially a control type could be created for an embedded AWT object; and made; a children of the receiving composite. There is a precedent for that with; OleFrame. That control could either be found from the Composite#_getChildren or; Composite#_getTabList and feed the getChildren normally. Or reference to the; frame coudl be kept as a member of the control and injected into the Children.; In addition; this could be an opportunity standardize the semantics of the AWT; frame creation with something like new AwtFrame(Composite parent) and; deprecating the old way using SWT_AWT.new_frame.; I do not know is if there is native way to get a Frame once created using; natives; but the frame should have a OS handle I guess; and could make its way; as a control.; Just some wild thoughts.; ; BTW; I have not looked into the SWT in AWT but I guess the pb may be similar but; not as an important use case IMHO.

description: I created the editor plugin which allows users to drop files on it; but; I have a problem with the editor on Linux when more than two documents are ; opened at the same time. ; On Windows; It works perfectly.; ; ===================== sample code ===============================; ------------------ MyTextEditor.java ----------------------------; package dnd.test;; ; import org.eclipse.swt.custom.StyledText;; import org.eclipse.swt.dnd.*;; import org.eclipse.swt.widgets.Composite;; import org.eclipse.ui.editors.text.TextEditor;; ; public class MyTextEditor extends TextEditor {;     public void createPartControl(Composite parent) {;         super.createPartControl(parent);; ;         // add drop support;         final StyledText styledText = getSourceViewer().getTextWidget();;         DropTargetAdapter dropAdapter = new DropTargetAdapter() {;             public void dragOver(DropTargetEvent event) {;                 event.detail = DND.DROP_COPY;;             };             public void drop(DropTargetEvent event) {;                 String[] filenames = (String[])event.data;;                 styledText.setText(filenames[0]);;             };         };;         Transfer[] transfers = {FileTransfer.getInstance()};;         DropTarget dropTarget = new DropTarget(styledText; DND.DROP_COPY);;         dropTarget.setTransfer(transfers);;         dropTarget.addDropListener(dropAdapter);;     }; }; ; -------------------------- plugin.xml ---------------------------; <?xml version=1.0 encoding=UTF-8?>;       <import plugin=org.eclipse.ui/>;    </requires>; ;    <extension;          point=org.eclipse.ui.editors>;       <editor;             name=My Text Editor;             icon=icons/test.gif;             extensions=txt;             ; contributorClass=org.eclipse.ui.texteditor.BasicTextEditorActionContributor;             class=dnd.test.MyTextEditor;             id=dnd.test.MyTextEditor>;       </editor>;    </extension>; </plugin>; ----------------------------------------------------------------

title: [Forms] DetailsPart.getKey() flawed
description: Hi!; ; I believe that  org.eclipse.ui.forms.DetailsPart.getKey()  will not function; properly without a page provider.; ; The Eclipse Forms Programming Guide shows ; org.eclipse.ui.forms.DetailsPart.registerPage()  being passed a Class object as; a key for the pages Hashtable. When a page provider has not been set; getKey(); simply uses Object.getClass() against the passed object. Even though the Class; passed to registerPage() and the Class returned from Object.getClass() refer to; the same class; the Class objects are different. This wouldnt matter if Class; implemented equals() and hashCode() but it doesnt. Instead; Class inherits; Object.equals() which checks for reference to the same object resulting in a; failure of the pages Hashtable to return a PageBag in; for example;; DetailsPart.showPage().; ; If a page provider is set; it can do something like:; ;   public Object getPageKey(Object object);   {;     return object.getClass();;   }; ;   public IDetailsPage getPage(Object key);   {;     IDetailsPage dp = null;;     if (key instanceof Class);     {;       Class clsKey = (Class)key;;       if (clsKey.isAssignableFrom(MyDetailsData.class)  && ; MyDetailsData.class.isAssignableFrom(clsKey));         dp = myDetailsPage;;     };     return dp;;   }; ; ; Jeff Lawson

title: [Contributions] <with variable=selection> does not fire when cursor position changes
description: This may seem like a strange thing; that I would worry about cursor changes; but consider inside a handler:; ; <handler ...>;        <activeWhen>;           <with variable=selection>;             <test property=com.foo.myNamespace.myProperty/>;           </with>;        </activeWhen>; </handler>; My presumption (and experience) seems to be that the tester associated with com.foo.myNamespace is only fired when the selection has changed. So lets consider an example order of operations:; ; 1. Select a range in an editor: this triggers the property tester.; 2. Select a new range in the editor: this triggers the property tester.; 3. Click in the editor; so it deselects the current selection; but no text is selected: this does not trigger the property tester.; ; Why not? This is a bit of a problem; because the activeWhen isnt reevaluated. Reconsider those three steps; with a little more detail:; ; 1. Select a range in an editor: this triggers the property tester; which fails; so the menu is not active.; 2. Select a new range in the editor: this triggers the property tester; which passes; so the menu is now active.; 3. Click in the editor; so it deselects the current selection; but no text is selected: this does not trigger the property tester. The cursor is inside a range that; if selected; would fail.; ; That last sentence is the important one: In other words; the lack of reevaluation means that the menu (which in my specific case is a context menu) will actually be incorrect.

description: Indexing is currently performed on first search attempt. If the product is ; large; this can take a long time; resulting in a frustrating initial search ; experience.; ; Ideally; local help should be indexed on first startup in the low-priority ; background thread. Products can elect to register a startup plug-in and tell the help ; system to initialize from there.; ; We propose to add the new API init() to both IHelpSystem and ; AbstractHelpSystem types. title: [EAP] No way to store UI-State like in 3.x with IMemento
description: The current EAP does not allow to persist the state in a way RCP 3.x allowed save the state by implementing IViewPart#saveState(). ; ; In EAP we only have @PreDestroy as a lifecycle which is not good because at this moment e.g. SWT-Widgets are already disposed and saving their state in ApplicationElement.persistedState is not possible any more.; ; My suggestion would be to:; a) add @PersistState annotation to ui.di; b) call it in the ContributedPart renderer in disposeWidget; ; Please not this make it work a bit different than in 3.x where the saveState was called on Workbench shutdown only which always bugged me there already.

title: [DataBinding] missing SetChanged notification
description: We set up a somewhat complex data binding scenario; where we need to manage multiple computed collections together.; ; With list implementations; we simply put ComputedLists into a MultiList; and everything works as expected. On the other hand; when putting ComputedSets into a UnionSet; we experience missing change notifications.; ; After some debugging; we found that the change notifications are not propagated properly between the ComputedSets and UnionSets; and we also managed to create a short application that reproduces it: ; ; https://gist.github.com/ujhelyiz/6124893/325ec18738ff6d679e4d3b37c8713294521ee6be; ; Our basic problem is that the ISetChangeListener of the UnionSet is not called if the change originates from a ComputedSet; however; each case the Sets are queried; the result is correct.; ; We are not sure whether we missed something; or maybe we found a bug in JFace Data Binding.; ; (Originally from http://www.eclipse.org/forums/index.php/mv/msg/496665/); ; Additional details:; As far as we see; the ComputedSet.makeDirty is called when there is a change; it calls makeStale() and during that the StalenessListeners (which are registered by the UnionSet probably) are called; at some point during the listeners; the calculate() method is called on the ComputedSet; which overwrites cachedSet with the new values. When makeStale() returns in makeDirty; the value of cachedSet is used as the oldSet but at this point; cachedSet already contains the new values and the difference will be empty.

title: Make EditionSelectionDialog.setHelpContextId API
description: 20060131; ; Some actions in jdt.ui are using setHelpContextId on EditionSelectionDialog.  setHelpContextId() is declared on ResizableDialog which is a super class of EditionSelectionDialog but not in an API package. title: Table.getItem(Point) only works for SWT.FULL_SELECTION style
description: In the code below; a MouseListener that is listening for mouseDown events on a ; Table; attempts to translate the coordinates of the point clicked on into a ; reference to the TableItem underneath the mouse click using Table.getItem; (Point). This only works if the Table has been constructed with the ; SWT.FULL_SELECTION style. Otherwise; it works only for mouse clicks over the ; first column of the Table - mouse clicks over subsequent columns result in ; Table.getItem(Point) return null.; ; Using 3.1M4; ; ------8<----; import org.eclipse.swt.SWT;; import org.eclipse.swt.events.MouseAdapter;; import org.eclipse.swt.events.MouseEvent;; import org.eclipse.swt.graphics.Point;; import org.eclipse.swt.layout.FillLayout;; import org.eclipse.swt.widgets.Display;; import org.eclipse.swt.widgets.Shell;; import org.eclipse.swt.widgets.Table;; import org.eclipse.swt.widgets.TableColumn;; import org.eclipse.swt.widgets.TableItem;; ; public class TableGetItemBugDemo {; ;     public static void main(String[] args) {;         Display display = new Display();;         Shell shell = new Shell(display);;         shell.setLayout(new FillLayout());; ;         // Change the style of the Table from SWT.NONE to SWT.FULL_SELECTION;;         // and it works OK.;         final Table table = new Table(shell; SWT.NONE);; ;         TableColumn columnOne = new TableColumn(table; SWT.LEFT);;         columnOne.setText(Column 1);;         columnOne.setWidth(200);; ;         TableColumn columnTwo = new TableColumn(table; SWT.LEFT);;         columnTwo.setText(Column 2);;         columnTwo.setWidth(200);; ;         TableItem itemOne = new TableItem(table; SWT.NONE);;         itemOne.setText(new String[] { 12345; Beware the Jabberwock });; ;         table.addMouseListener(new MouseAdapter() {;             public void mouseDown(MouseEvent event) {;                 Point point = new Point(event.x; event.y);;                 TableItem item = table.getItem(point);;                 System.out.println(Mouse down at  + point + ; over ; TableItem =  + item);;             };         });; ;         shell.pack();;         shell.open();;         while (!shell.isDisposed()) {;             if (!display.readAndDispatch());                 display.sleep();;         };         display.dispose();;     }; }; ------8<-----

title: PluginActivator.ensureNormalStartup() is a bogus check
description: Im not sure what the intention of ensureNormalStartup() is.  But it seems to ; be a bogus check in the PluginActivator.  Here is my understanding of the code.; ; It checks to see if the startlevel of the framework is <= to the startlevel of ; the bundle that is starting.  If it is then an exception is thrown which ; prevents the bundle from starting.; ; There is no way the startlevel of the framework can be less than that of the ; bundle.  If it was then the bundle would not be starting.  If the startlevels ; are equal why do we bail?; ; There is a case where you can make every plugin that uses PluginActivator fail ; to start if you set the following properties in the config.ini; ; osgi.startlevel=6; osgi.bundles.defaultStartLevel=6; ; This will cause the startlevel of the bundle to always be equal to the ; startlevel of the framework which will cause it to not start because of ; ensureNormalStartup().  Can we just remove the call to this method?  In the ; eclipse adaptor we made it so that eclipse Auto-started plugins never have the ; persistent start bit set.  This should prevent the bundles from starting even ; after a crash.

title: LineStyleListener: weird concept; really a LineStyleProducer
description: The concept of a LineStyleListener is weird.; ; The communication goes; primarily; from a LineStyleListener to the StyledText; widget (the listener tells the widget which styles should be set on it); which; makes it really counterintuitive to call the style producer a listener... its; really more of a producer; and the StyledText widget is the real listener. ; Thus; I think that LineStyleProducer is a better choice for a name than; LineStyleListener.  If tell a random person that there is a widget and an; object that figures out what styles to put on the widget; and then you ask; him/her which one they think is the LineStyleListener; I bet they would say that; its the widget.; ; Similarly; one usually thinks of an event as the transmission of information; from a producer to a consumer.  However; a LineStyleEvent is more of a reverse; transmission; since its the listeners responsibility to set a field in the; event object that is given to it and have that information be transmitted back; to the widget incidentally.  It would make much more sense here if the widget; just called a method on a LineStyleProducer called StyleRange[]; getLineStyles(int line).; ; In summary; it would be better to have a setLineStyleProducer() method; taking a; LineStyleProducer class as argument.  Or maybe instead; a setLineStyleStore(); method and LineStyleStore class; akin to the ITextStore class in JFace.

title: ExtensionsParser key translation can call RegistryStrategy.translate() with incomplete key
description: Build ID: I20080617-2000; ; Steps To Reproduce:; Say in your plugin.xml you have a translation key named %translationKey as an element value (not as an attribute) where the % character happens to be the 2043rd character in the file.; ; ExtensionParser.characters() gets called in 2048 character chunks.  So the first time it gets called; it will parse the key as %trans.  It will look up this key using the supplied RegistryStrategy.; ; When the RegistryStrategyOSGI class doesnt find a requested key; it just returns that key as the translated string.  And in the end; this works fine; because when the next 2048 character chunk is passed to ExtensionParser.characters(); its smart enough to realize that the current key is not completely translated yet; so it retries with the now completed key and replaces the value from the previous iteration.; ; However; if someone were to provide a different RegistryStrategy that throws a MissingResourceException when the translated key is not found (which seems like a reasonable thing to do); the Exception will bubble up and cause problems.; ; The logic in ExtensionParser.characters() should be changed so that the RegistryStrategy will not get invoked with partial keys.; ; Bug 75592 is closely related and contains an attached plugin.xml that can help reproduce the problem.

description: Steps to reproduce:; 1. Write a simple plugin with a button in the toolbar and an action handler associated.; 2. In the action handler; in the dispose method throw a runtime exception; e.g. NullPointerException; 3. Start the Eclipse IDE with the plugin; 4. title: [KeyBindings] M8 keybinding not working as expected
description: Under M8 if I try and bind the key seq Ctrl+E to Delete line it does not work; under some circumstances.; Steps to reproduce:; Go to key config dialog.; Select Category Text Editing; Select Name Delete line; Add key sequence Ctrl+E and pick When: Editing text; Click Apply and/or OK; Edit a java file and try hitting Ctrl+E - it does not work. Ctrl+D does however.; Now go back into key bindings and change the binding for Ctrl+E so it applies; when: Editing Java source. It now works.; ; Since Editing text is a superset of Editing Java Source I would expect the; original binding to work.

description: This is basically the complement to Bug 50914; which dealt with initializing the; Apply Patch wizard.; ; 1. Start the wizard to create a new patch.; 2. Select Save in File System; 3. title: [WorkingSets] Separate workingSets from UI code
description: This is a request to separate the concept of a workingSet from being tied to UI code; thus allowing non UI based code to cleanly work with workingSets avoiding a dependency on the UI plugins.; ; For example; we (a product building on Eclipse) provide a tool that can perform headless (Ant based / non UI) based builds.  A portion of the tool has the capability to setup the workspace prior to running the build.  One of our customers would like to use this capability to setup developer environments.  Their use case would be something like: ; ; 1) Execute script pointing at a clean workspace; 2) Set workspace preferences by importing an .epf or other.  ; 3) Import projects from version control system using a .psf file. ; 3a) This would include setting up workingSets as defined by the same .psf file.; ; Although thinking longer term; if the workingSets werent tied to UI; they could potentially be used for defining sets that could be used to perform builds or other non UI based actions.; ; mike.

title: Eclipse fails to detect new plugins in extension locations
description: There are two ways to install Eclipse plugins: using update sites; and by copying folders in to the plug-in directory. Although the former; is nicer; there are many plguins out there that dont provide update sites and so rely on the latter method.; ; I like to put all my plugins into an extsnio location; so I van upgrade my core Eclipse without plugin side effects. Unfortunately; Ive been noticing that Eclipse is unable to detect new plugins in an extension location; unless they are installed via an update site. Thus; I am forced to put them in with the core.; ; An extension location should be treated like the core plugins folder. On restart with -clean; it sghould be re-scanned for new plugins.
